title: Auve Tech launches driverless airport shuttle service without onboard safety operator
source_used: Robotics & Automation News (fulltext, carries Auve Tech's announcement)
key_facts: Auve Tech demonstrated its MiCa shuttle at Tallinn Airport, Estonia, without an onboard safety operator, with remote supervision.
Auve Tech received authorisation in August 2026 to remove the onboard safety operator from its passenger service there.
MiCa is an eight-passenger electric Level 4 shuttle using cameras and LiDAR.
It carries Magnetic MRO's staff and equipment between hangars, about 1,000 km a week at an average autonomy rate of 99.9 percent, per the company.
Cooperation began in 2023; commercial operations began in 2025.
One remote supervisor can watch several vehicles, which the company says lowers costs.
The company and airport say it is the first airport in Europe authorised to run an autonomous vehicle without an onboard safety operator.
quote_evidence: Auve Tech received authorisation in August 2026 to remove the onboard safety operator from its passenger service at Tallinn Airport.
Today, MiCa shuttles connect Magnetic MRO facilities on the airside cover approximately 1,000 kilometres per week with an average autonomy rate of 99.9 percent.
Remote supervision enables one supervisor to oversee several vehicles and intervene only when needed, rather than assigning one driver to every vehicle.
why_it_matters_hint: Removing the person on board is what makes driverless shuttles cheaper to run.
notes: Company and airport claims; 'first in Europe' is their own statement. Day of the August authorisation is not stated.
